column3: NKJV has “Joseph and His mother,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “His father and mother.”
NKJV has “about eighty-four years,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “until eighty-four years.” NKJV supplies “God.”
NKJV has “to the Lord,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “to God.”
NKJV has “their own city,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “their city.”
NKJV includes “in spirit,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “became strong, filled with wisdom.”
NKJV has “Joseph and His mother,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “His parents.”
NKJV has “about My Father's business”; the Greek “in the things of My Father” may also mean “in My Father's house.”
